relationships.title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Herron and others challenged Presbytery’s decision to proceed to trial after a BCO 31-2 finding, his administrative suspension, denial of access to Presbytery records and meetings, and a public statement. The SJC sustained only the access issue: suspension from official functions did not remove his membership rights, though it did not entitle him to every investigative-committee document. Finding no clear error on the other issues, it ordered trial to proceed, temporarily stayed censure decisions, and postponed related complaints through trial and any appeal.

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt.

relationships.title: Flesher and Weekly v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: In Complaint 2015-03, Steve Flesher and Randy Weekly challenged Metro Atlanta Presbytery, but the SJC did not reach the merits. Because the issues raised had already been adjudicated in Appeal 2015-08, the SJC declared Complaint 2015-03 moot and approved that disposition. The short decision thus records a mootness ruling based on prior appellate adjudication; the underlying presbytery action and the Appeal 2015-08 decision are not described in the supplied text.

metadata.synopsis: Thompson used a BCO 43 complaint to challenge his Session indictment during an ongoing disciplinary case, according to the separate concurrence. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order. It held that a defendant must raise such objections during process in the court of original jurisdiction under BCO 32-14 and, if still dissatisfied, pursue them on appeal under BCO 42-3. The ruling did not decide the indictment objection’s merits.

metadata.synopsis: Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint.

G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery, which failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case, causing irremediable injury. The SJC did not reach the merits; it suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, rebuked Pacific Presbytery, and urged greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. Dismissal therefore did not leave the challenged judgment enforceable. A separate concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions.

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed convictions and indefinite suspension arising from conflict over Presbytery's direction that he resign. The SJC upheld all three convictions, finding two procedural errors nonprejudicial and rejecting the other preserved challenges. But Presbytery could not treat its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship as authority to compel resignation on pain of discipline. The SJC therefore vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for reconsideration of censure; Grady's separate administrative suspension remained effective.

relationships.title: Paul W. Lee v. Korean Southwest

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it.

metadata.synopsis: Smith appealed discipline for divisiveness, gossip and slander, broken membership vows, and contumacy arising largely from complaints and letters during church conflict. The SJC sustained her appeal, reversed guilt on all four charges, and annulled suspension from the sacraments. The documentary record proved none of the allegations; filing complaints was not itself divisiveness, and the trial improperly lacked a witness, shifted proof to Smith, showed prejudice, and unfairly rejected her written defense. The SJC declined remand because the evidence was insufficient.
